title: In a jam, need some advice...

posts.author: BNTKids-Studios
posts.body:
Hello! I'm wanting to make a specific game I have in mind, but I don't have a way to test out certain features or see them in action the way I am visualizing or hoping they will work for RPGMaker MZ or MV.
I am working on other things right now (paying off car problems, etc) but while I do this, I want to test certain features of RPGMaker MZ and MV and decide which route is best for me.
However, I already somehow used up the free trial of MZ AND MV and I thus, I cannot test said program and features.
I also need to test out some plugins before I buy them, namely Dragonbones Integration and some other plugins. However, these plugins cost money, and I currently don't have $$$ to throw around trying to test various plugins! I don't actually know when I will be able to test them!
I (might) have an artist who wants to work with me, provided I can afford their prices. Before I delve into paying this artist tho, I need to figure out what assets I'll need, and get a price quote and figure for all these assets. In order to do this, I need to test out the programs and plugins to see what works best for my project, then buy those plugins and use them base for the artist to see how my project is going to look gamewise, so they can decide the best route, artwork, and prices for me.
In the end, if things continue the way they are, I might be spending hundreds of dollars to "test" every plugin out there that relates to my needs, before finding the correct one! And that's spendy...
How would you guys proceed with this?
Sorry, I'm not a great problem solver! Bear with me!
TL;DR: Game Creation Problem (Loop): Artist Price Quote > Assets Needed > Game Style Visualized > Software & Plugin Testing Needed > Not Enough Money to test them all > Delay in Game Asset Creation and Artist Price Quote

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
I would map out every system that you need, and than look at both engines and see which has the cheapest/best plugins for each.
At that point, I would make a decision as to which engine would be the cheapest or most effective. Also, assets can come way later. Just use placeholders for now.
You could also give an overview of the systems needed and ask other people if they've done similar things, with which plugins/engines etc.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: I dunno. To me it sounds like you should be taking care of more important things than making a game. Especially when your financial situation is as dire as you describe it.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
MV is only $12 when it goes on sale (pretty much every month) and has more free plugins than MZ, and Yanfly suite is a lot cheaper than VisuStella.
If you can't even afford $12 then I guess use a free engine like Godot or freemium like GDevelop.

posts.author: BNTKids-Studios
posts.body:
Ok. I see a bunch of plugins on yanfly wiki.
How does this program stack up with layering and overlapping tiles? I also need to factor this in if I am going to make a game. Mv seems to have no layers system from what people are saying. I come from an rpg maker xp era and thus I am only familiar with layered tilesets. If mv had a lack of layering, I may have to commission even more assets to make my game, an asset for each unique iteration of a tiles appearance, including overlaps.

MV doesn't have layering built into the editor but MZ does. There is an iOS app that lets you edit MV or MZ maps that has the layering built in. I hear you can also do layering with Tiled but I haven't tried it.
